title: Per-tenant threshold calibrator with streak-tolerance and safe switchover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a per-tenant circuit threshold calibrator that adapts trip points using streak-tolerance and Bayesian smoothing. Goals: 1) reduce noisy trips due to transient spikes, 2) keep global SLOs intact during region failovers, and 3) ensure safe fallback to pre-authorized cheaper model variants or stateless fallthrough handlers. The calibrator runs online per-tenant and per-dependency, producing a time-windowed trip threshold and a confidence score. When confidence is low we use conservative hysteresis and slow-roll switchover; when high, we allow aggressive shedding. The system cooperates with multi-region failover: it publishes lightweight health vectors so regional controllers can make consistent decisions without central coordination.
acceptance_criteria: Calibrator publishes per-tenant trip thresholds and confidence scores to /internal/circuit-calib API within 200ms
False-positive trip rate (measured as trips leading to <10s additional tail latency) reduced by >=40% in our STO workload compared to fixed thresholds
During a simulated region failover (fail primary region), requests are routed to fallback region and SLO degradation <5% for 10 minutes
Safe fallback path exists for each tenant: (1) model-variant downgrade, (2) stateless text-only handler, (3) 503-with-grace JSON with retry-after — implemented and exercised in chaos tests
Rollout can be toggled via per-tenant feature flag and has automatic rollback on increase in error budget burn-rate > 2x baseline
design_decisions: Use Bayesian Exponential Moving Average (BEMA) over fixed quantile windows to estimate baseline latency and error rates per tenant
Introduce 'streak-tolerance' counter that requires N consecutive high-quantile observations before lowering threshold; N is tenant-weighted (low-volume tenants get higher N)
Separate 'safety' and 'performance' thresholds: safety triggers immediate soft-shed to stateless fallback, performance triggers model-variant downgrade
Publish small health vectors (latency_q95, error_rate_5m, confidence) via topic://circuit-health for lightweight regional sync
Fallback selection uses pre-ranked per-tenant affinity list to avoid cold-cache penalties (prefer cheaper model hosted in same region first)
Hysteresis windows scale with confidence score: confidence <0.6 => multiply hysteresis by 2
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal dogfood tenants (20) enabled in canary region for 48h; monitoring dashboards instrumented
Stage 2: 5% of small-volume customers across two regions for 72h; evaluate false positives and cache miss rate
Stage 3: Ramp to 25% of customers by traffic, run region-failover chaos experiment
Stage 4: Full rollout with automatic guardrail (rollback on error budget burn spike) and postmortem window for 72h
test_plan: Unit tests for BEMA estimator and streak counter boundary cases
Integration test simulating bursty tenants with synthetic latency spikes and backend model OOMs
Chaos test: kill primary region inference pods and validate multi-region switchover and calibrator convergence within 90s
Load test: 10k rps mixed tenants; measure trips, fallback rates, and end-to-end latency distribution
notes: We must avoid per-request per-tenant DB reads; thresholds are cached in memory with TTL 30s and persisted to redis for recovery
Estimate assumes existing circuit mesh shims (ENG-33478) provide a hook to read thresholds; minor shim required to accept confidence score
Operator UI will show per-tenant confidence and last_changed timestamp — Ops asked for ability to pin an emergency threshold
We will add telemetry tags: calibrator_version, streak_count, confidence_bucket for easier aggregation
